title: Imperfect Synthetic Controls
headline: Open finding: Under A1-A5, the imperfect synthetic-control estimator is asymptotically unbiased for the treatment effect.

claims.label: Theorem 4.1 asymptotic unbiasedness
claims.gist: Under A1-A5, the imperfect synthetic-control estimator is asymptotically unbiased for the treatment effect.
claims.statement: Under A1-A5, the imperfect synthetic-control estimator is asymptotically unbiased for the treatment effect.
conditions: Assumptions A1-A5, including existence of at least one all-period-valid synthetic relation.
Weights are estimated from pre-treatment moment conditions and may be nonunique.

result.summary: A1-A5 identify only a pre-treatment weight class; observationally equivalent DGPs give treatment effects separated by 3/5 because post-period predictions vary across that class.
result.witness: A1-A5 identify only a pre-treatment weight class; observationally equivalent DGPs give treatment effects separated by 3/5 because post-period predictions vary across that class.
result.argument: Five-unit construction, A1-A5 audit, all-unit moment network, exact observational equivalence and sharp invariance condition. Limits: Does not show every application or every nonunique-weight design is invalid.
not_claimed: The theorem can survive under uniqueness or post-period invariance across the pre-fit set.

evidence.detail: A fresh separate-session hostile validation supports the stated finding; its scope and limits are summarized above.
